embassy-building.definition: The building where a country's diplomatic mission works in another country.
embassy-building.exampleUsage: Visitors entered the embassy building through the main gate.

flag-pole.definition: A tall pole from which a flag is flown.
flag-pole.exampleUsage: The national flag flew from the flag pole outside the embassy.

national-flag.definition: An official flag represents a country at government institutions, schools, and public events.

security-gate.definition: A controlled entrance used to check people or vehicles before allowing access to a protected place.
security-gate.exampleUsage: Everyone passed through the security gate before entering the compound.

guard-booth.definition: A small enclosed shelter where a security guard can sit or work near an entrance.
guard-booth.exampleUsage: The guard checked the visitor's ID from the guard booth.

reception-hall.definition: A large room used for receiving guests or holding formal gatherings.
reception-hall.exampleUsage: The ambassador greeted the guests in the reception hall.

waiting-room.definition: A room where people sit until they are called, admitted, or served.
waiting-room.exampleUsage: Applicants waited quietly in the waiting room.

conference-room.definition: A room in a school or office set aside for organized meetings and formal discussion.

courtyard.definition: An area wholly or partly surrounded by walls or buildings.

passport.definition: Any authorization to pass or go somewhere.

visa.definition: To provide (a passport) with a visa.

application-form.definition: A document with set questions and spaces for people requesting admission, work, services, or financial help.

identity-card.definition: An official card used to confirm the holder’s identity.

birth-certificate.definition: A copy or extract of a birth certificate, authenticated by the civil registry, provides official proof for immigration, school enrollment, or identity checks.

photograph.definition: A picture made with a camera to record a person, place, or event.

stamp.definition: A carved or raised object used to print the same design repeatedly.

seal.definition: A stamp affixed to a document (as to attest to its authenticity or to seal it).

letter.definition: A written message addressed to a person or organization.

envelope.definition: The maximum operating capability of a system (especially an aircraft).

computer.definition: A machine for performing calculations automatically.

printer.definition: (computer science) an output device that prints the results of data processing.

telephone.definition: A device used to speak with someone who is far away.

fax-machine.definition: A device that sends and receives copies of documents through a telephone or communications line.
fax-machine.exampleUsage: The office used the fax machine to send the signed form.

scanner.definition: A device that turns a paper image or document into a digital file.

filing-cabinet.definition: A piece of furniture used to store documents in drawers.

safe.definition: Free from danger or the risk of harm.

shredder.definition: A device that shreds documents (usually in order to prevent the wrong people from reading them).

laminator.definition: A person who makes laminates (especially plastic laminates).

security-camera.definition: A camera used to watch or record an area for safety and security purposes.
security-camera.exampleUsage: The security camera recorded everyone entering the lobby.

metal-detector.definition: A device that signals when metal is nearby, helping check food for stray pieces or locate metal buried underground.

x-ray-machine.definition: A device that produces X-rays, allowing images of structures inside the body.

security-guard.definition: A person who protects a building and its people.

badge.definition: An emblem (a small piece of plastic or cloth or metal) that signifies your status (rank or membership or affiliation etc.).

visitor-pass.definition: An official card, badge, or document that gives a visitor temporary permission to enter a place.
visitor-pass.exampleUsage: Reception gave each guest a visitor pass for the day.

turnstile.definition: A gate consisting of a post that acts as a pivot for rotating arms.

alarm-system.definition: A device or network of devices that identifies dangers such as break-ins, fires, or equipment problems and then issues a sound, light, or remote alert.

intercom.definition: A communication system linking different rooms within a building or ship etc.

bulletproof-glass.definition: Laminated glass made with inner layers that absorb the force of bullets and help stop them.

ambassador.definition: A diplomat of the highest rank.

consul.definition: A diplomat appointed by a government to protect its commercial interests and help its citizens in a foreign country.

diplomat.definition: An official engaged in international negotiations.

secretary.definition: A person who is head of an administrative department of government.

translator.definition: A person who translates written messages from one language to another.

protocol-officer.definition: An official who organizes formal visits and ceremonies and ensures that diplomatic procedures are followed.
protocol-officer.exampleUsage: The protocol officer arranged the order of greetings for the ceremony.

cultural-attach.definition: An embassy official who works to develop cultural, educational, or artistic relations with the host country.
cultural-attach.exampleUsage: The cultural attaché organized an exhibition for local students.

legal-advisor.definition: A person with legal expertise who gives advice about laws, rights, contracts, or official decisions.
legal-advisor.exampleUsage: The embassy asked its legal advisor to review the agreement.

driver.definition: A golfer who hits the golf ball with a driver.

receptionist.definition: A secretary whose main duty is to answer the telephone and receive visitors.

national-emblem.definition: An officially approved symbol expresses a country’s authority and character, appearing on government seals and national promotional materials.

map.definition: A drawing that shows places, routes, and geographical features.

globe.definition: A round model or map of the Earth.

clock-with-time-zones.definition: A clock or display that shows the current time in several different regions of the world.
clock-with-time-zones.exampleUsage: The lobby has a clock with time zones for major world capitals.

painting.definition: A picture made with paint and shown on a wall.

sculpture.definition: A three-dimensional work of plastic art.

book.definition: A set of printed pages bound together for reading.

certificate.definition: To present someone with a certificate.

plaque.definition: (pathology) a small abnormal patch on or inside the body.

application.definition: The act of bringing something to bear.

identification.definition: The condition of having the identity (of a person or object) established.

form.definition: A category of things distinguished by some common characteristic or quality.

interpreter.definition: (computer science) a program that translates and executes source language statements one line at a time.

guard.definition: An adult who watches children to keep them safe.

clerk.definition: To work as a clerk, as in the legal business.

attach.definition: To take temporary possession of as a security, by legal authority.

flag.definition: A piece of cloth attached to a pole as a symbol.

reception.definition: (American football) the act of catching a pass in football.

ceremony.definition: A formal event performed on a special occasion.

treaty.definition: A written agreement between two states or sovereigns.

negotiation.definition: A discussion intended to produce an agreement.

alliance.definition: An organization of people (or countries) involved in a pact or treaty.

summit.definition: The highest level or degree attainable.
